mechanism_narrative: The observed consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -32.9% to -26.7% over the last four weeks, indicates a sustained recovery trend that will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases or remains flat compared to the last 28 days, indicating a reversal or stagnation of the recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, indicated by a weekly increase of at least 0.5 percentage points for two consecutive weeks, will lead to increased weekday foot traffic in retail areas, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 0.5 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Despite WORKPLACES rising by at least 0.5 points for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent upward trend in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests a return to pre-pandemic commuting behaviors, which will collectively drive a stronger recovery in RETAIL_REC as people integrate shopping into their daily routines over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue their upward trend, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days declines or remains stagnant, the interaction effect is disproven.

mechanism_narrative: As the RESIDENTIAL mobility index continues its gradual decline, indicating less time spent at home, this behavioral shift will free up more time for out-of-home activities, directly contributing to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 10.0 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 10.0, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase compared to the previous 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The recent strong increase in PARKS mobility, rising by 5.3 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w, indicates greater outdoor activity and a general increase in out-of-home movement that will spill over into nearby retail and recreation areas in the immediate short term, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases compared to the previous 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent positive and increasing trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, from 0.9% to 3.7% over the last four weeks, reflects a growing public confidence in out-of-home activities, which will translate into increased discretionary spending and visits to retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains positive and increasing, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days declines or stagnates.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing PARKS mobility signifies a shift from home-centric activities to outdoor and public space engagement, which will indirectly encourage more visits to retail and recreation spots over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases while PARKS mobility increases, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not show an upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across multiple mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, PARKS) suggests an underlying easing of public health restrictions or a shift in policy messaging, which will continue to encourage out-of-home activities and boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite continued recovery across multiple mobility categories, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days declines, indicating that policy changes are not effectively translating into sustained retail activity.
